mainTopic: Believing a woman about her child's or husband's lineage: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע, ברי versus שמא, and one doubt versus a ספק ספיקא
overview: An ארוסה became pregnant, and her ארוס admitted the child was his. רב יוסף rules the child is kosher for two reasons: the ארוס admits it, and the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, who believes the woman. אביי objects that שמואל said not to act on רבן גמליאל's view unless most men around her are kosher, and for an ארוסה most men are not. The answer is that שמואל's limit is only לכתחילה, and a pregnancy that has already happened counts as בדיעבד. Next, אביי asks רבא how רבי יהושע can say the woman is not believed, when he himself permitted an אלמנת עיסה to marry a כהן. רבא first answers that a bride checks her husband's family, but then notes that this answer makes רבן גמליאל contradict himself. So רבא gives a new answer: רבן גמליאל decides by the woman's claim (ברי versus שמא), and רבי יהושע decides by the number of doubts (one doubt versus a ספק ספיקא). The amud ends with a ברייתא defining an אלמנת עיסה, and רבי מאיר's view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ארוס admits the child is his
steps.stepSummary: The ארוס answers 'yes, from me': he admits the baby his ארוסה is carrying is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, she became pregnant from me.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes a story that began just before this part of the text. The ארוס is asked whether his pregnant ארוסה's baby is his, and he says yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His admission matters a great deal. If the father is the ארוס, the child is not a ממזר, because she is his own ארוסה and their relationship is not a forbidden union. This admission becomes the first reason in רב יוסף's ruling in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
From me
A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: Yes, from me.
phrases.notes: The ארוס is answering the question asked just before this line: is the baby his?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a case story that started before this part of the text.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ארוס says the child is his.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules the child is kosher, for two reasons
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף sees no reason to worry. First, the ארוס admits he is the father. Second, שמואל ruled that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, who believes the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Why should we worry about her? First, he admits it. And besides, רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל that the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his ruling: the child is kosher. He gives two separate reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason one is the ארוס's own admission. Reason two is wider: even without an admission, רבן גמליאל (in the משנה) believes a woman who says the child is from a kosher man, and שמואל rules like him. Giving the second reason suggests רב יוסף thinks רבן גמליאל would declare the child kosher even if the ארוס did not admit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Why should we be worried about her?
First... and besides (two separate reasons)
Admits
The final law follows...

steps.whyThisMatters: The second reason sets up the whole argument that follows: is רבן גמליאל's view strong enough to rely on in a case like this?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
About what should we be worried for her?
First, since he admits it.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And besides, didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case just described.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child is kosher, both because the ארוס admits it and because the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: אביי: שמואל said not to act on רבן גמליאל here
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges the second reason. שמואל told רב יהודה not to act on רבן גמליאל's view unless most men around her are kosher. Here most men around her are not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: In this case, if he did not admit it, would רבן גמליאל really call the child kosher? But שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Sharp one, the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל, but do not act on it unless most of the men around her are kosher.' And here, most of the men around her are not kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's second reason. He argues that רבן גמליאל's ruling would not help in this case without the ארוס's admission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל himself limited רבן גמליאל's ruling: in practice, rely on it only when most men nearby are kosher. For an ארוסה, almost every man is 'not kosher' for her, because a child from anyone except the ארוס would be a ממזר. So, אביי argues, the second reason does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה; it may mean 'sharp one' or 'big-toothed one'
Do not act on it in practice
Most of the men around her are kosher
Not kosher, or a forbidden match for her

steps.confusionAlert: 'Most men around her are not kosher' does not mean the men are bad people. It means that, for her, a child from any of them (other than the ארוס) would be a ממזר.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And in this case, when he does not admit it,
does Rabban Gamliel declare the child kosher?
But didn't Shmuel say to Rav Yehuda:
Shinana, the halacha follows Rabban Gamliel,
but you should not act on it
unless most of the men around her are kosher.
And here, most of the men around her are not kosher!
phrases.notes: Since she is an ארוסה, a child from any man other than the ארוס would be a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּבְהָא, כִּי לָא מוֹדֵה מַכְשַׁר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second reason of רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's use of 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל' as a reason in this case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל limited acting on רבן גמליאל's view to cases where most men around her are kosher. For an ארוסה, most men around her are not.

steps.title: Turning the question back on אביי
steps.stepSummary: The reply points out that שמואל's statement looks self-contradictory if read אביי's way: how can something be 'the הלכה' and yet 'don't act on it'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, the statement itself should bother you: 'It is the הלכה, but do not act on it'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The reply to אביי begins by turning his question around. It shows that שמואל's statement needs explaining anyway, which sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'do not act on it' means 'never rely on it,' then calling it 'the הלכה' makes no sense. So שמואל must have meant something narrower. This opens the way to a better reading of his words.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
It should be difficult for you
The statement itself

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: The text doesn't name the speaker; this is the answer to אביי, given by רב יוסף.

phrases.english: the statement itself should be difficult for you:
'It is the halacha, but you should not act on it'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on אביי's reading of שמואל by showing it leads to a contradiction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's reading of שמואל's limit as an absolute rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Read that way, 'it is the הלכה' and 'do not act on it' contradict each other.

steps.title: לכתחילה versus בדיעבד: this case counts as בדיעבד
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's two statements apply to different situations. 'Don't act on it' is for לכתחילה; 'it is the הלכה' is for בדיעבד. A pregnant ארוסה is like בדיעבד, so we rely on רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what must you say? This is for לכתחילה, and that is for בדיעבד. And this case, too, is like בדיעבד.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the answer. שמואל's warning only applies before the fact, and the pregnant ארוסה counts as an after-the-fact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Don't act unless most men are kosher' is a guideline for when nothing has happened yet. Once there is already a pregnancy, the child is here, and refusing to believe her would brand him a ממזר. That is a בדיעבד situation, so שמואל's ruling like רבן גמליאל applies, and רב יוסף's second reason stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what must you say?
From the start, before acting
After the fact, once it has already happened
It is considered like an after-the-fact case

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's limit on רבן גמליאל applies only לכתחילה. When a child is already on the way, the case counts as בדיעבד and we rely on the woman's claim.

phrases.english: Rather, what must you say?
This is before the fact, that is after the fact.
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is 'don't act on it'; the second, 'that', is 'the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל'.

phrases.english: And this case too is like after the fact.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר: הָא לְכַתְּחִלָּה, הָא דִּיעֲבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 4, and with it אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two situations: לכתחילה versus בדיעבד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought שמואל's limit blocks relying on רבן גמליאל whenever most men around her are not kosher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit applies only לכתחילה. A pregnant ארוסה is like בדיעבד, so the child is kosher.

steps.title: אביי asks רבא: doesn't רבי יהושע trust the woman elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out a contradiction. In our משנה, רבי יהושע says the woman is not believed. Yet רבי יהושע testified that an אלמנת עיסה may marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised a contradiction to רבא: Did רבי יהושע really say she is not believed? But compare this: רבי יהושע and רבי יהודה בן בתירא testified about an אלמנת עיסה that she is permitted to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. אביי sets רבי יהושע's view in our משנה against another source where רבי יהושע seems lenient in a case of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, רבי יהושע does not rely on the woman's word to make her kosher. In the עדות, he allows an אלמנת עיסה, a widow from a family whose lineage is in doubt, to marry a כהן. So in that case he is lenient despite the doubt, and the question is how the two fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him
And compare it with this (an opposing source)
Testified, in a formal report of a הלכה
A widow whose husband came from a family with doubtful lineage
Permitted to marry a כהן

phrases.english: Abaye raised a contradiction to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת?
phrases.english: Did Rabbi Yehoshua really say she is not believed?
And compare it with this:

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira testified
about the widow of an 'isa' family,
phrases.notes: An 'עיסה' is a family whose lineage is in doubt, literally 'a dough' that is mixed together.

phrases.english: that she is permitted to marry into the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: whether רבי יהושע contradicts himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling in our משנה that the woman is not believed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the עדות about אלמנת עיסה, רבי יהושע is lenient even though the lineage is in doubt. That seems to clash with his strictness about the woman in our משנה.

steps.title: A bride checks; a woman acting immorally does not
steps.stepSummary: The answer to אביי: the two cases are not alike. A woman who marries checks her husband's family first, but a woman acting immorally does not check her partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare them?! There, a woman who gets married checks out the family first and then marries. Here, does a woman acting immorally check first and then act immorally?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's contradiction in רבי יהושע: the widow case and our case are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the אלמנת עיסה case, the woman married the man, and a bride normally looks into the groom's family before the wedding. So we can trust that the marriage was fine. In our משנה, the woman was with an unknown man, and nobody checks a partner's lineage in that situation, so רבי יהושע is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (literally, 'is it like this now?')
She checks / investigates
She gets married
Acts immorally (relations outside of marriage)

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!
There: a woman who gets married
checks first and then marries.
Here, a woman who acts immorally,
does she check first and then act immorally?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's contradiction in רבי יהושע from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's leniency for the widow should also apply to the pregnant woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: A bride checks her husband's family, so we can rely on her marriage. A woman acting immorally does not check, so we are strict.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל also seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: why only ask about רבי יהושע? רבן גמליאל also contradicts himself. In the widow case he would not let a court rule leniently, but in our case he believes the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is it only רבי יהושע against רבי יהושע that is hard, and רבן גמליאל against רבן גמליאל is not hard? But the end of that משנה teaches: רבן גמליאל said to them: We accept your testimony. But what can we do? רבן יוחנן בן זכאי decreed not to set up a court for this, because the כהנים listen to you to push a woman away, but not to bring her close.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new problem. The answer in step 7 fixes רבי יהושע, but now רבן גמליאל looks like he contradicts himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 7, the widow case should be the easier, more lenient one. Yet רבן גמליאל holds back there and will not let a court allow her to a כהן. In our משנה he is lenient and believes the woman. So the 'she checks' answer cannot explain רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The end clause of a משנה
We accept your testimony
Decreed
To push away (rule a woman forbidden)
To bring close (rule a woman permitted)

phrases.english: Rava said:
Is it only Rabbi Yehoshua against Rabbi Yehoshua that is difficult,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא?
phrases.english: and Rabban Gamliel against Rabban Gamliel is not difficult?
But it teaches in the end clause:
Rabban Gamliel said to them:
We accept your testimony,
but what can we do,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי גָּזַר רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: for Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai decreed

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹשִׁיב בֵּית דִּין עַל כָּךְ,
phrases.english: not to set up a court for this,
because the priests listen to you to push away
but not to bring close.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קַשְׁיָא, דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 7 leaves רבן גמליאל contradicting himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'a bride checks' answer of step 7, and רבן גמליאל's consistency.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the widow case is easier, רבן גמליאל should not hold back there while being lenient in our harder case.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: a sure claim versus a doubt
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer for רבן גמליאל. In our case the woman makes a sure claim (ברי). In the widow case there is only a doubt (שמא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רבן גמליאל against רבן גמליאל is not difficult. There, it is a sure claim; here, it is only a maybe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the earlier approach and explains רבן גמליאל in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the woman says for certain that the man was kosher, so רבן גמליאל believes her. In the widow case nobody really knows. The doubt is in the facts themselves, and she has no sure claim to rely on, so he is careful.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer)
A sure, certain claim
A 'maybe'; an unsure situation

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'there' (הָתָם) means our משנה, and 'here' (הָכָא) means the widow. That is the opposite of how the words were used in step 7.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel against Rabban Gamliel is not difficult:
There, it is certain; here, it is a maybe.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the pregnant woman who says for sure the man was kosher. 'Here' is the widow, where nobody knows for sure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אַדְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 8 with a new distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל is lenient in our case but strict in the widow case, so he seems to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: He believes a woman's sure claim. He does not rely on her when the situation is only a doubt.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: one doubt versus two doubts
steps.stepSummary: רבא also explains רבי יהושע. Our case has only one doubt, so he is strict. The widow case has two doubts, so he is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע against רבי יהושע is also not difficult. There, there is one doubt; here, there are two doubts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes by explaining רבי יהושע with a new distinction of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the pregnant woman there is one question: was the man kosher or not? So רבי יהושע is strict. With the widow there are two questions. Is her husband the doubtful member of the family? And even if he is, maybe that person is not a חלל at all. With two doubts, רבי יהושע is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
One doubt
Two doubts

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final answers: רבן גמליאל relies on a sure claim (ברי) but not on a doubt (שמא). רבי יהושע is strict with one doubt but lenient with two doubts.
steps.whyThisMatters: These are two basic rules for handling doubt: a sure claim carries weight, and two doubts together can lead to leniency.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua against Rabbi Yehoshua is also not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — חַד סְפֵיקָא, הָכָא — תְּרֵי סְפֵיקֵי.
phrases.english: There, there is one doubt; here, there are two doubts.
phrases.notes: Again, 'there' is the pregnant woman and 'here' is the widow.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אַדְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's new approach and now resolves אביי's original contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (one doubt versus two doubts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע is strict here but lenient with the widow, so he seems to contradict himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: With one doubt he is strict. With two doubts he is lenient.

steps.title: Summary: what each תנא treats as strong and as weak
steps.stepSummary: רבא's answer is summed up. For רבן גמליאל, a ברי claim outweighs any doubt, and a שמא claim is too weak even with a ספק ספיקא. For רבי יהושע, a single doubt outweighs even a ברי claim, and a ספק ספיקא is enough even with a שמא claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: So, for רבן גמליאל: a sure claim is so strong that even with one doubt he says she is fit. A 'maybe' claim is so weak that even with a double doubt he says she is unfit. For רבי יהושע: one doubt is so strong (it makes him strict) that even with a sure claim he says she is unfit. A double doubt is so weak (it lets him be lenient) that even with a 'maybe' claim he says she is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up רבא's answers from the last two steps by laying out each תנא's full system side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא looks at a different factor first. רבן גמליאל asks: is the woman's claim ברי or שמא? The number of doubts does not change his ruling. רבי יהושע asks: is there one doubt or a ספק ספיקא? The kind of claim does not change his ruling. This is why neither of them contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore / so
It is strong for him (it decides the case for him)
It is weak for him (it does not decide the case for him)
A single doubt
A double doubt: two separate doubts, each of which could make her fit
Declares fit / declares unfit (here, to marry a כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל decides by the TYPE OF CLAIM (ברי beats שמא). רבי יהושע decides by the NUMBER OF DOUBTS (a ספק ספיקא is lenient, a single doubt is strict). This settles both contradictions raised by אביי and רבא.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Strong' here does not always mean lenient. For רבן גמליאל, ברי is strong in a lenient direction. For רבי יהושע, a single doubt is strong in a strict direction. 'Strong' just means 'this is the factor that decides the case.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the basic idea behind the whole מחלוקת: two different ways to weigh doubt, either by the person's claim or by how many doubts there are.

phrases.english: Therefore, according to Rabban Gamliel:
a sure claim is strong for him,
so that even with only one doubt he declares her fit.
And a 'maybe' claim is weak for him,
so that even with a double doubt he declares her unfit.
phrases.notes: This is the אלמנת עיסה case from step 8, where רבן גמליאל would not rule leniently.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yehoshua: a single doubt is strong for him,
phrases.notes: Here 'strong' means a single doubt is enough to make him strict.

phrases.english: so that even with a sure claim he declares her unfit,
and a double doubt is weak for him,
so that even with a 'maybe' claim he declares her fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts together the two answers of רבא (steps 9 and 10) into one complete system for each תנא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן גמליאל follows ברי vs. שמא no matter how many doubts there are. רבי יהושע follows one doubt vs. ספק ספיקא no matter what the woman claims. So neither contradicts himself.

steps.title: A ברייתא defines which widow counts as an אלמנת עיסה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines an אלמנת עיסה as a widow from a family with no doubtful ממזרות, נתינות, or ancestry from royal slaves. Then רבי מאיר begins to give his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who is an אלמנת עיסה? Any family that has no problem from ממזרות, no problem from נתינות, and no problem from royal slaves. רבי מאיר said:
steps.whatsHappening: Since the אלמנת עיסה came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that defines exactly what kind of family this is. At the end it starts quoting רבי מאיר, whose words continue in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיסה is a 'mixed' family with some doubt in its lineage. The ברייתא limits which doubts count: a widow from this family may still marry a כהן only if the doubt is not about ממזרות, נתינות, or royal slaves. These three are more serious kinds of doubt, so they do not fall under the lenient ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow from a family whose lineage has some doubt (literally 'widow of a mixed dough')
Being a ממזר, a child born from a forbidden relationship
Being a נתין, a descendant of the גבעונים, who may not marry into the Jewish people
Royal slaves: kings' servants who could take Jewish women by force

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ברייתא says an אלמנת עיסה has no doubts at all. The family is still an עיסה with some doubt. The ברייתא only rules out these three serious kinds of doubt.

Who is a widow of a family of mixed lineage?
Any family that has in it no problem
not because of mamzer status,
and not because of Gibeonite status,
and not because of kings' slaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of the two תנאים to define the term אלמנת עיסה, which came up in רבי יהושע's testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אלמנת עיסה, who may marry a כהן, is a widow from a family with no doubt of ממזרות, נתינות, or descent from royal slaves.
